title: The Magic Stone That Was Tested on a Prisoner
style: Stylized realistic 3D CGI animation still, high-end animated explainer look, Pixar-meets-realism, cinematic soft lighting, detailed skin, hair and fabric, expressive faces, shallow depth of field, no text, no letters, no gore, vertical 9:16 framing.

sections.name: The Magic Stone That Was Tested on a Prisoner

lines.prompt: A 1500s French royal court, a king in rich robes holding up a smooth dark stone, courtiers watching in awe

lines: For centuries, rich Europeans paid fortunes for a magic stone. A bezoar.

lines.prompt: A cutaway of a goat showing a smooth round stone in its stomach, soft glowing light

lines: Bezoars are hard lumps that form in the stomachs of animals like goats. They were believed to cure any poison.

lines.prompt: 1567 royal court, a surgeon in black robes with a beard arguing with the king while pointing at the stone

lines: In 1567, the king's surgeon, Ambroise Paré, said he thought it was nonsense. So they tested it.

lines.prompt: A prison cell, a nervous cook in chains being offered a deal by a guard, candlelight

lines: A cook was due to be executed for stealing. He was offered a deal. Take poison, then the stone. If he lived, he'd go free.

lines.prompt: The cook lying ill on a straw bed in a cell, the surgeon kneeling beside him, sad expression

lines: He took the poison, then the bezoar. Hours later, he died.

lines.prompt: Paré holding up the stone and shaking his head in front of the king, who looks embarrassed

lines: The bezoar did nothing. It's one of the first recorded experiments testing a medicine.
